title: La carretera
goal: Break down between towns and get help from strangers
culture: Somebody will stop. Asking a stranger on the road for a tow is completely ordinary, and Dios se lo pague — the biggest thank-you there is — is exactly what this situation is for. You last heard it from the woman with the suitcases.

beats.es: (Un carro se orilla detrás de usted.) ¿Qué pasó, amigo?
beats.good: Se me quedó — it stopped on me. The me puts it on you without making it your fault, which is exactly the right amount of blame.
No arranca — it will not start. Two words that will get somebody’s head under your bonnet within a minute on any road in this country.

beats.es: (Se asoma al motor un rato.) Uy. Eso es taller.
beats.en: Could you give me a tow?
beats.good: Un jalón is a tow or a lift. Asking a stranger on the road for one is completely ordinary, and he had already stopped before you asked.

beats.es: Va pues. Amarre ahí y vamos despacio hasta Nandaime.
beats.good: The largest thank-you there is, and the one the woman with the suitcases used on you at the terminal. This is the situation it exists for.
